title: GRTeclyn research fork — traversable wormholes and the Bondi dipole
description:
Code, run matrices and packed campaign data behind The Bondi dipole in full numerical relativity: a self-accelerating positive–negative mass binary (v2), Rotation slows the instability of Ellis–Bronnikov wormholes and Binary Ellis–Bronnikov wormholes in 3+1 numerical relativity: mergers, fly-bys and gravitational waves (N. M. Shirokov and I. Nachevsky, 2026).

This version (v2.0-bondi-dipole) carries the Bondi dipole paper's v2 data: the 24 simulations of a positive- and a negative-mass boson star, rerun with fourth-order time integration and corrected initial data, with their time series, parameter files, launch records, figures and the scripts that redraw them (results/bondi-dipole-runaway).

A GRTeclyn (AMReX/GPU) research fork with a Python orchestration layer: a spectral solver for stationary rotating Ellis–Bronnikov wormholes, checked against identities it never uses; their 3+1 evolution with a background-relative outer boundary; constraint-solved and exactly boosted binaries of drainholes held open by a ghost scalar; CCZ4 evolution with refinement boxes that follow the throats, a spectral MOTS finder, Weyl-scalar and scalar-flux extraction; two complex scalar fields of opposite gravitational sign for the Bondi pair; and the analysis and figure scripts. Includes the solver's solutions, the parameter files and diagnostic streams of every run the papers use, the run registries and the figures — reproducible without a GPU.
